Subject: Request: Quarterly invoicing + staggered remit for Redwood subscription

Hi Priyom / Vanessa,

Thanks again for the demo last week — the team is excited to move to pilot. Our procurement team has one ask before we sign: due to our internal fiscal calendar and APAC cashflow windows, we need Redwood to issue quarterly invoices that can be paid in three staggered remittances across each quarter (30/60/90 days). Practically, that would look like: Redwood issues one invoice per quarter, and we remit 1/3 immediately, 1/3 at 60 days, and 1/3 at 90 days.

We understand this is non-standard. We can accept a conditional service hold if a tranche is late, and we are happy to provide a corporate credit form and a purchase order. Can this be approved on the commercial side? Our go-live target is 2027-09-15.

Attachments: Skyline_SOW_v3.pdf (proposal), Skyline_credit_form.xlsx (vendor info)

Best,
Maya Patel

Team — forwarding Skyline's request for an exec decision. Key facts:
- ARR for pilot (first 6 months) ~ $110k ARR equivalent, expansion potential to $600k ARR in 12 months.
- Customer requests: invoice quarterly, Redwood to accept 3-way staggered remit per quarter (1/3 immediate, 1/3 at 60d, 1/3 at 90d).
- They will provide PO and credit form (attached).
- Region: APAC; they cite local treasury cycles and bank settlement delays (esp. August monsoon bank holidays).

Questions for approval:
1) Does Finance accept a rolling quarterly invoice with split remits (three tranches) without additional collateral (they propose conditional service hold on missed tranche)?
2) Is Sales authorized to offer a 2% early-pay discount if they switch to monthly billing instead? (not their preference)
3) Any contractual language we need to add for late-tranche penalties or suspension?

Rishi — can you run a quick credit check and recommend guardrails (e.g., ACH only, escrow, or prepaid buffer)?

Ive attached Skyline_SOW_v3.pdf and their credit form.

Thanks,
Priyom Das
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference
From: rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai
To: priyom_das@redwood.ai; lauren_bishop@redwood.ai; vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai
Date: Wed, 4 Aug 2027 02:11:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Fwd: Request: Quarterly invoicing + staggered remit for Redwood subscription

Quick finance review — summary below.

Credit: Skyline is a mid-size regional health provider, last 12mo revenue public filings look stable; procurement submitted corporate bank guarantee is standard. Recommend: accept the staggered remit with these guardrails:
- Redwood issues a single quarterly invoice; payment schedule recorded in SOW and invoice terms (1/3 due on receipt, 1/3 due 60d, 1/3 due 90d).
- Require a payment method that supports traceability (USD wire or corporate ACH).
- Add a 2% late fee on missed tranche after a 15-day grace period, and right to suspend service after 30 days overdue for any tranche.
- Collect a one-time security deposit equal to the first tranche for the pilot (apply to first invoice).

Risk note: APAC banking holidays can push actual receipt dates; recommend contract clause allowing for bank processing delays but not indefinite delay.

If Sales wants to push discount for monthly billing, cap discount at 2% and require monthly invoice cadence.

Rishi
VP, Finance Ops
From: lauren_bishop@redwood.ai
To: priyom_das@redwood.ai; rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai; vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai
Date: Thu, 5 Aug 2027 18:20:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Fwd: Request: Quarterly invoicing + staggered remit for Redwood subscription

Thanks Rishi — that sounds reasonable. I'm supportive of the guardrails with one operational tweak: because Skyline is in APAC and we have cross-border FX exposure, require the security deposit to be held in USD and cleared before provisioning. Also, add an explicit milestone in the SOW tying pilot activation to deposit clearance.

Approval recommendation to Execs: allow Sales to accept staggered remit for pilot under the listed guardrails (security deposit = first tranche, 2% late fee after 15 days, suspension after 30 days). No additional discount at this stage.

Priyom / Vanessa — if you can get confirmation from Skyline on their chosen payment rail and sign-off on the SOW language, I will push this as an approved exception and prepare the addendum.

Best,
Lauren Bishop
Head of Sales, Enterprise Accounts
From: Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.ai>
To: Maya Patel <maya@skyline-health.com>; Arjun Menon <arjun.m@skyline-health.com>
Cc: vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai; lauren_bishop@redwood.ai; rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 9 Aug 2027 17:30:00 +0000
Subject: Approved: Staggered remit for pilot (terms & next steps)

Hi Maya / Arjun — good news: Redwood has approved a pilot with the staggered remit structure under the following conditions:

1) Redwood will issue one invoice per quarter; Skyline will remit 1/3 on receipt, 1/3 at day 60, and 1/3 at day 90.
2) Skyline to provide cleared USD security deposit equal to the first tranche before provisioning.
3) Payment rails: wired USD transfer preferred (or corporate ACH where available).
4) Late tranche policy: 15-day grace, then 2% late fee; if any tranche is 30+ days overdue Redwood reserves the right to suspend service until arrears are cleared.
5) No discount offered for staggered remit; a 2% early-pay discount can be discussed if Skyline switches to monthly invoices.

Next steps:
- Maya / Procurement: confirm bank details and sign the addendum (DocuSign link) by 2027-08-12 to keep the planned 9/15 go-live.
- Redwood: vanessa will update the SOW and attach the addendum; finance will issue the first invoice once deposit clears.

DocuSign: https://docusign.net/exec-approvals/DL-9763
HubSpot deal: https://app.hubspot.com/deal/9763

Appreciate the flexibility — excited to get the pilot started.

Thanks,
Priyom Das
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference
